children: MUMBAI: Indian IT stocks surged on Friday, with the Nifty IT index gaining more than 3%, as investors brushed aside fresh uncertainty over the US government's move to bar eight technology companies from participating in a programme linked to employment-based green-card applications.

OpenAI's lower-than-estimated revenue run rate and Tata Consultancy Services' relatively firm second-quarter results also helped boost sentiment in the sector, which has been beaten down by worries about AI-related disruptions to its business model. The Nifty IT index's rise on Friday was its biggest single-day gain since August 28.

TCS shares rose 4.2%. HCL Technologies and Infosys gained around 3% each, while Wipro rose about 2.7% and Tech Mahindra advanced around 1.5%. "The rally in Indian IT stocks appears to reflect factors beyond TCS' Q2 results, which offered some reassurance on earnings resilience but no clear demand inflexion," said Kunal Bajaj, research analyst at Choice Institutional Equities. - Our Bureau GREEN CARD FREEZE Tanya Pandey& Surabhi Agarwal New Delhi: The four Indian IT services companies suspended by the United States Labour Department from the employment-based green card process--Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Wipro and HCLTech--together recorded just 61 certified Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) filings in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 (Oct 1, 2025-June 30, 2026), with HCL America recording 59 certified cases and TCS only two.

Infosys and Wipro had no recorded cases in the period and neither did US-headquartered Cognizant. In the previous fiscal year, the number for the top Indian IT companies was 1,429. An ET analysis of US Department of Labour data shows that while American technology companies are bigger users of the programme, which allows foreign workers on H-1B visas to apply for permanent residency or the green card, employers in non-tech sectors such as food, meat and seafood were among the programme's biggest users.

TCS CEO K Krithivasan told ET on Friday that the suspension would have no impact on the company's business model or delivery of client projects, noting that its applications to convert H-1B visa holders to green-card holders had been in the single digits annually over the past two years. "We have close to 40,000 people in the US, and more than 50% of them are permanent residents or citizens," he said, adding that TCS files such applications occasionally when clients want the company to retain an employee for the long term. Foreign workers can stay in the US on an H-1B visa for six years, after which they have to return or apply for a green card.

Consider the data for fiscal 2025. Of the 15 largest filers that year, five were technology companies and 10 were non-tech employers. Microsoft was the only technology company among the five biggest PERM filers, recording 3,153 cases. The remaining top four were food company FPL Food (2,260 cases), seafood producer Consolidated Catfish Producers (1,733), while JCG Foods of Georgia and South Georgia Pecan Company each recorded 1,387.

Apart from Microsoft, major technology filers included Apple (1,239 cases), Oracle America (1,222), Intel (1,033) and Salesforce (812). The pattern continued in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, when Microsoft recorded 1,680 cases and healthcare firm Management Health Systems had 1,393.

Adobe recorded 183 cases, of which 182 were certified. PERM filings for both Microsoft and Adobe were also suspended, along with Cognizant and the four Indian IT firms. The "vast majority of Microsoft employees in the United States are Americans," the company said in response to ET's query.

Of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications it filed last fiscal year, 80% were to extend or change the status of existing employees. "These were not to hire new people. The remaining applications were for individuals already legally in the US and accounted for about 1% of its US workforce," the company said in its statement. The US Department of Labour on Thursday suspended Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCLTech and Capgemini from the PERM programme.

It stopped accepting new applications and halted processing of pending cases for the companies, alleging that the programme had been used to replace American workers with lower-paid foreign labour. India, in response to the announcement, said the suspension would not, by itself, affect existing H-1B visas or the status of visa holders and their dependents, although it could impact eligible employees' green card applications.

title: Indian IT PERM Filings Were Down Before Curbs
